long_sentences.sentence: Filtering a right-table column for a non-null value in the WHERE clause can accidentally turn your LEFT JOIN back into an INNER JOIN, silently erasing your unmatched rows because the WHERE filter evaluates after the join and excludes the newly padded NULL values [S12].

1.quote: If a record exists in one table but has no corresponding match in the other, it is completely filtered out and excluded from your results.

2.quote: The syntax lists the first table, declares the INNER JOIN keyword alongside the second table, and uses an ON clause to define the matching criteria.

3.quote: In reality, a left join only guarantees that all rows from the left table are kept. Unmatched rows from the right table are still excluded unless you use a FULL JOIN.

4.quote: INNER JOIN: Combines rows from multiple tables based on a matching condition, returning strictly the intersecting records and dropping unmatched rows

items.question: How do you properly construct an INNER JOIN query in SQL to combine 'employees' and 'departments' tables based on 'department_id'?
options: SELECT * FROM employees JOIN departments MATCH employees.department_id = departments.department_id;
SELECT * FROM employees INNER JOIN departments ON employees.department_id = departments.department_id;
SELECT * FROM employees, departments USING INNER JOIN department_id;
SELECT * FROM employees INNER JOIN departments WHERE employees.department_id = departments.department_id;

INNER JOIN only works with numerical keys, while LEFT JOIN handles text strings.

confusions.quote: Relational databases store data across separate, normalized tables to reduce redundancy
confusions.why: I have no idea what normalized tables or redundancy mean since they aren't explained anywhere.

confusions.quote: This operation finds the strict mathematical intersection of both datasets
confusions.why: Taking this literally, I started thinking about math class geometry instead of tables.

confusions.quote: Filtering a right-table column for a non-null value in the WHERE clause can accidentally turn your LEFT JOIN back into an INNER JOIN, silently erasing your unmatched rows because the WHERE filter evaluates after the join and excludes the newly padded NULL values.
confusions.why: This part is way too complicated with too many big words, and I got totally mixed up about whether WHERE or ON is supposed to be used.

confusions.quote: Filtering a right-table column for a non-null value in the WHERE clause can accidentally turn your LEFT JOIN back into an INNER JOIN, silently erasing your unmatched rows because the WHERE filter evaluates after the join and excludes the newly padded NULL values.
confusions.why: This part is a bit heavy and confusing about why a WHERE clause suddenly changes the whole join type when I just wanted to filter something.

confusions.quote: When performing a LEFT JOIN where a row in the right table has no corresponding match in the left table, what is returned for the left table's columns in that row?
confusions.why: This is a trick question or a conceptual confusion because a left join by definition always preserves the left table, so rows in the left table are never missing when matched against the right table; rather, it is the right table rows that are missing.

rubric.justification: The lesson strictly addresses writing inner/left joins and predicting output rows for missing data.

Python-based list comprehensions effectively simulate relational join outputs for students.
